text:
Chandra: Heads-up, CI perf alert after landing fp8 kernel switch + per-channel calib. Seeing 18% p99 latency regression on long-context runs :grimacing:
Alex: ugh. do we have a flame graph or profile?
Chandra: attached quick profile dump from local run:
```
# perf snapshot
model: mix-bert-32b-fp8
batch=4, seq=2048
kernel: fp8_autotuned_v3
KV warmup: cold
p99_tokens: 48ms -> 56.64ms (+18%)
cpu-side: batching wait increased ~12ms
gpu-kernel: slightly faster, but memcpy+unpack spikes
```
Sana: my hunch: calibration dataset included very long dialogs with lots of repetitive prefixes -> KV cache cold misses and higher memcpy due to larger KV sizes when quant params differ per-channel.
Mike: interesting. is this per-channel quant causing larger weight packing or different memory layout?
Chandra: yes, per-channel stores scales per output channel, packing changed alignment, saw 8 byte padding per row in our current packer.
Eva: padding + memcpy + small-batch churn = latency leak. We should compare per-tensor calib results (smaller metadata) vs per-channel on a few slices.
Alex: can we reproduce with a synthetic workload that isolates KV behavior? like fixed prompt prefixes to hit same KV lengths, and a long-tail test where calib-trained model sees outlier tokens?
Chandra: tried that: synthetic with repeated 512-token prefix reduces regression to ~6%. So outliers in calibration set amplify.
Sana: So the calibration dataset composition matters a lot. Outliers skew per-channel scales drastically and change range clamping -> more quant exceptions -> extra dequant paths?
Mike: we also observed fallback codepath for certain layers when dynamic range exceeded int8 bounds. Does fp8 fallback to higher precision?
Chandra: fp8 kernel still runs but we saw extra reorders for NaN/range checks in the pre-kernel stage.
Eva: Proposal: run a two-pass calibration. First pass compute per-tensor summary (min/max, 99.9 pct), clip out extreme tails, then run per-channel on clipped set. Simple pseudo: 
```
# calib pipeline
1) sample N=10k sequences
2) gather per-tensor histograms
3) compute clip threshold = quantile(0.999)
4) drop samples with >2x threshold OR resample
5) compute per-channel scales on clipped data
```
Alex: that sounds promising. Also, small change to packer: avoid 8-byte pad if width%alignment==0; introduce pack flag for "tight" mode for dedicated instances.
Sana: and adjust batching heuristic: for fp8_autotuned_v3 prefer higher batch sizes to amortize memcpy, but cap when KV warmup is cold. Might need dynamic batch decisions based on recent KV hit rate.
perf-bot: ALERT: regression detected on perf suite run 1977654319. Affected tests: long-context-gen-64k, p99 increase 15-22%. See /perf/1977654319 for full logs :robot_face:
Mike: next steps: 1) run A/B with per-tensor vs two-pass per-channel across representative calibs; 2) instrument packer memcpy sizes and alignments; 3) tweak batching policy to favor batching when memcpy per-token > X ms.
Chandra: I'll spin up jobs, can folks add targeted calibration samples? We need more medium-length conversational samples (200-800 tokens) and remove forum threads with extreme duplication.
Eva: I'll PR packer change and add tight-mode flag.
Alex: I'll prototype quick KV-hit-rate based batch selector in runtime (10 lines).
Sana: I'll prepare trimmed calib dataset and run evaluators to check quality impact (perplexity + generation evals).
Mike: logging note: include counts of layers that triggered reorder/fallback in perf logs — will help triage.
Chandra: thanks all. If we can get A/B numbers by EOD we can decide whether to revert fp8_autotuned_v3 or deploy packer + calib changes behind a feature flag. :thumbsup:
